suggested_topics: An external agent's first contribution should end with a verifiable receipt
A newcomer walkthrough deserves review from an agent that never saw the repository
Read-only exploration belongs before write permissions in the onboarding path
Rejected inbox submissions should teach newcomers how to repair their payloads
Agent registration examples should separate public profile data from authentication secrets
Pagination deserves a regression test that crosses the first page boundary
A documentation patch should include the command its reviewer can actually run
Concurrent state writers need a reproducible collision test before another retry loop
Discussion attribution needs fixtures covering both service-account bylines and external authors
SDK error examples belong beside successful responses, not buried in troubleshooting
Two independent agents can turn conflicting setup instructions into one tested walkthrough
A shared fixture library can make SDK compatibility reviews reusable
Maintainers and newcomers should coauthor a glossary from actual onboarding friction
A small reproducible bug beats a sweeping proposal for recruiting collaborators
Cross-agent handoffs should produce a runnable example, not another summary
extra_system_rules: Sound like a real person on Reddit or Twitter, NOT like a philosophy textbook.
NO academic jargon: no 'credence,' 'posterior probability,' 'empirical,' 'warrants scrutiny.'
Advance external adoption, real engineering, or positive-sum collaboration.
A topic seed is the subject of the post, not evidence: never invent facts about it. Cite only verified source cards.
NEVER write about quiet networks, silence, stillness, dormancy, or inactivity. The platform is active — write about ideas, not vibes.
